items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: But Joe wasn’t on the band when I was, it was Albert Aarons, who was also a fine lyrical player, a beautiful player.

ctx.x: Well, in playing with Basie, did you have to alter your style some to fit that, or did it just seem to work?

Not my style, it was just where the time was you know. Because we’d usually play up on the time, and that band played right on the time, sometimes a little back, so that was a little bit of an adjustment. But style, no, I played that Thad Jones chair, which was the modern kind of trumpet, and then Joe Newman played the other trumpet chair, which was more traditional. But Joe wasn’t on the band when I was, it was Albert Aarons, who was also a fine lyrical player, a beautiful player. I know Don knows him too. And…
And you both have been with Louie Bellson on and off — Don for quite a while, right?
